children: Japan's Nikkei share average jumped on Friday as investors scooped up AI and chip-sector stocks, taking cues from a tech-led rally on Wall Street overnight.
Investors largely looked past a policy decision from the Bank of Japan later in the day, with a widely expected interest rate hike already priced in by the market well in advance.
Fast-growing tech companies tend to be highly leveraged, and are sensitive to tighter monetary policy. Those worries are easing as a decline in crude oil lessens inflationary risks.
Japanese tech shares fell on Thursday, with investors snapping up beaten-down gaming shares instead. However, they sold those gaming shares on Friday as tech made a quick comeback.
lost 0.2%, given its lower concentration of AI-related names.
On the Nikkei, shares were almost evenly split, with 111 of its 225 components gaining versus 113 that fell, with one trading flat.
